steps.content: [Eastside Hospital, After the Assassination Attempt]
You enter the hospital room again. The flowers by the side of the bed bloom vibrantly, yet the woman lying in bed only stares off into the distance.

The apple is fresh and juicy. Your skills at peeling have improved quite a bit over these visits. Just as you're about to offer Clementine a slice, a gust of wind sweeps through the room, sending the handwritten manuscript on the windowsill into the air.
You quickly set down the knife and rush to catch the pages fluttering through the air.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: It's not that important, you know. I don't think I'll be continuing it anyway.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But I care about this story.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Then keep it. Think of it as a memento.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I'm frail and sickly, haven't the strength to hurt a fly, and I've lost my job to boot. I'll probably end up a vagrant at this rate... Guess I'll have to rely on you to keep me fed.
She takes the apple slices you cut and carves them into little rabbits, eating one herself before setting the other on the plate for you.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: How is it?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...They don't call you S-Class for nothing. The Bureau has always believed in specialized roles for specialized talents, you know. I don't see why we can't have someone whose sole job is carving rabbit apples.
After half an hour of forced small talk, Clementine looks at you with a gentle expression and indicates that visiting hours are over. She needs her rest, so you'll need to part here.
After leaving her room, you review her medical report once more. Physically, Clementine is fine—but her mental state is deeply concerning.
[Flashback]

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, here's the recent monitoring report on Sinner Clementine.

Nightingale's report spans three full pages. Written in it are detailed observations, which can be summarized into several key concerns: highly rigid behavior patterns, pronounced social withdrawal, declining interest and attention span, and a disconnect between her physiological indicators and actual behavior.

Aside from these signs of somatization, the data from her psychological and emotional monitoring software paints an equally concerning picture. Perhaps some form of intervention or counseling is in order.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Did she say anything?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: She only said... "I need time to adjust."
Why does that sound exactly like what you heard in the recording? Is this some kind of scripted response?

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: That's not all. Miss Clementine keeps forgetting what she's doing. Last time I went to discuss her new book with her, she was carrying an afternoon tea tray to the terrace. I called out to her, and only then did she realize the tray was completely empty!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If I recall correctly, she fainted from low blood sugar that time. We had to call a doctor to give her a glucose injection before she started feeling better.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Yup, that's the one. Chief, is something weighing on her mind?
[End of Flashback]
On the day of her discharge, you once again invite Clementine to accompany you somewhere.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Is this another new assignment? Or is it a new baiting operation?

options: This time, it's just an outing.

choices.text: This time, it's just an outing.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm just inviting you to take a walk with me. We do value work-life balance around here, after all.
As you talk, you come to a stop before a grand gate. It's the entrance to a school hosting an open day. A steady stream of parents, students, and visitors is flowing in and out.
After a bit of effort, the two of you now look like you came from just any other respectable middle-class family in Eastside.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: This is... a school?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yeah. Did you join any clubs when you were in school?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I dabbled in a few things, I suppose. Theater, murder mystery games, the detective club, and a taxidermy group.

options: Then this is the perfect chance to try something new.

choices.text: Then this is the perfect chance to try something new.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Come on, follow me.
You enter the classroom just as the bell rings. A public debate is underway.

steps.speaker: Opposition Debater
steps.content: ...Delayed justice is the same as self-consolation for the living. It may comfort the survivors, but it will never reach the dead. When justice misses its window, it loses all warmth and meaning...
Clementine raises an eyebrow. She looks up at the debate topic—
<size=45><color=#7683a2><b><i>"Is Delayed Justice Still Justice?"</size>

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: This... did you arrange this?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: No, it's just a coincidence. If I really wanted to force you to listen to some inspirational speech, I wouldn't go about it like this.

The debaters continue their back-and-forth on the stage. Their arguments can almost be called overused, and clearly, Clementine has little interest in listening. She's about to say something when you press a finger to your lips, gesturing for her to look at the stage.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Shh. The proposition's final debater is about to speak.
On the podium, a debater named Lydia commands the room's attention. Her clear voice carries across the hall, reaching your ears with perfect clarity.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: Then by your logic, should sheriffs stop investigating cold cases? Just because the truth no longer holds meaning for society?

steps.speaker: Opposition Debater
steps.content: Cold case investigations serve to fulfill institutional duty. Their core value lies in sending society a message that crimes will not be forgotten. It's nothing more than a form of deterrence and prevention, and cannot be called justice.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: But the very essence of justice is manifested through this systematic fulfillment of duty. Following your logic, trials in absentia for deceased criminals would be equally meaningless. Yet, we persist precisely because it affirms justice as an absolute value—one whose authority transcends life and death.

steps.speaker: Opposition Debater
steps.content: But that's merely solace for the living! When justice is reduced to psychological comfort for survivors, it undermines the sacred standard it should uphold—
Lydia blinks, catching a knowing look from her teammate.
A clever bait. You glance toward Clementine. Her eyes widen ever so slightly.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: The opposition seems to have reduced justice to immediate compensation for the individual. However, we believe the true meaning of justice lies in society's collective memory and covenant.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: It is through our relentless pursuit of it that humanity avoids slumbering in its mistakes for eternity.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: In pursuing delayed justice, we have to fight against time and oblivion. Still, we persist in this struggle so that next time, justice might arrive before tragedy strikes.
The bell rings soon after. The young woman's closing statement was brilliant. Applause fills the room, lasting long after she finishes. Many in the crowd cheer and whistle, calling out Lydia's name.

Lydia lets out a long breath from the podium. She runs over to shake hands with each of her opponents, then turns to the crowd with a playful bow, rubbing her flushed cheeks, still warm with excitement.
People continue to discuss the debate and what activities they'll attend next as they slowly file out of the classroom in an orderly fashion. Clementine remains transfixed, staring at the stage.

You follow Clementine's gaze. Lydia sits on the edge of the podium, legs swinging freely, completely at ease. She looks exactly as someone her age should—beaming with a radiant smile as she watches the audience exit.
She raises her arm high, revealing extensive burn scars. You know that Clementine recognizes the girl too. <color=#fb9259>She's the child she saved all those years ago.</color>

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...So this is your real aim.

options: Why don't you take a guess?

choices.text: Why don't you take a guess?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If you guess right, I'll tell you the answer.
You use Clementine's own spell against her. She shakes her head with a rueful smile in response.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: Excuse me, sorry to interrupt. Are you two here with family?
A clear voice suddenly rings out beside you. Lydia has appeared at your side without either of you noticing, her sharp gaze moving between you and Clementine.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: We were just discussing the debate. It's been so long since I've been on campus, I got a little carried away... My apologies, were we being disruptive?
Clementine's smile remains polite and composed, but you notice her hands are clasped tightly together. It's barely perceptible, but it seems like she's holding something back.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: Oh, I see! I noticed you two in the audience earlier, but you didn't strike me as students or parents. Did you perhaps come all the way here because you were interested in the debate?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We're actually here to check out the school for our little sister.
You take over, smoothly delivering the cover story you prepared in advance. Your words sound earnest, your tone sincere.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: She received an offer of admission from Eastside University, but she's still feeling lost about what to do next. That's why we wanted to hear from students here about how they found their path and goals.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What about you? What made you want to come to this school?
Lydia thinks for a moment, then scratches her head sheepishly.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: It's a little embarrassing to admit... but I actually spent some time at an orphanage when I was younger. There was this older girl there—her dream was to come to this school.
You glance at Clementine. She's looking at Lydia with an unusual intensity, complex emotions churning in her eyes.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Did she... end up coming here to study?
Lydia nods emphatically, beaming.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: Of course she did! She was incredible! But I was pretty young back then, so I don't remember much from before I got adopted... Oh, but I heard she got her acceptance letter really early, and she even published a novel.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: She used to read to us when we were little. We all loved her stories—it was like the orphanage would turn into this magical world of adventure at night.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: Hehe... I've never actually seen her around campus, but I'm happy just knowing we're connected like this.
The girl's smile is contagious. You find yourself smiling too. A burn scar marks the side of her face, but she doesn't hide it. Perhaps to her, it's akin to a badge of honor.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So you came to this school because of her? Do you want to be a novelist like her?

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: Nope! I want to become a chief prosecutor!

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: ...Something happened at my orphanage. I was too young to understand what it meant back then.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: But later on, I found out that the truth was uncovered and the people responsible were punished! That's why I switched to law—I want to join the judicial system after graduation and uphold justice myself.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...But that's just one case. Far more injustices are never brought to light, and many of the guilty walk free.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: What if... there was a way outside the rules? A more effective means to put an end to all of it? Would you still choose this path?
There's a familiar edge to her voice. It's nothing like the casual, detached tone she had with you earlier. You can tell she's being serious now.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: That's alright.
Lydia doesn't hesitate. Her answer is resolute.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: I may still be in school, but I understand that our legal system is fragile. There are countless forces driven by anger and hatred that could tear it down with ease.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: In the debate earlier... Someone also brought up the question of whether the law is worth defending if it can't deliver what people hope for right away. If it can't punish the guilty and protect the innocent, doesn't that make upholding it meaningless?

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: And to that, my answer will always be no. I choose to believe that justice, however delayed, will come. The law is built on our collective longing for justice. It's not just the law that's protecting us, we are also protecting it.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: That's exactly why I will walk straight ahead towards my goal, no matter what.
Lydia places her hand over her chest. This time, you see it clearly—the scars on her arm from the fire, being shown without shame.
The memory of that baby tooth unbidden. Its owner once said her dream was to grow up quickly.

What did that mean to her back then? Before the fire, before the scars... It meant a small window glowing in the moonlight. It meant those adventure stories that never seemed to end. It meant the tall, sturdy trees in the courtyard that always offered shade in the summer heat.
Brush aside a thin layer of soil and a few leaves, and there they were—dreams large and small, buried solemnly beneath the tree.
No one taught her how to grow up, but she learned by watching that girl. Perhaps the path Clementine once walked... she walked it too.
Through the tides of loneliness and darkness, she endured. And now, at last, she stands before you.
Clementine listens with that same faint smile as Lydia speaks with conviction. Then, she suddenly becomes self-conscious and rubs her arm.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: Oh! Sorry, I got a little too into it. Looks like I'm still in debate mode from earlier. Haha.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: I know I'm just some naive girl fresh out of the gate, completely oblivious to how dark the world really is. My words might not hold any substance, and my classmates also tell me that I'm too idealistic, too stubborn about all this...

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: But I believe that progress, whether in law or society, depends on people who are naive enough to dream and brave enough to act. And if that's what it takes, then I'll gladly be one of them!

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: I think... whether it's her or everyone else from the orphanage... they'd all support my decision. They'd be proud of me!
The girl's eyes shine with such conviction, so bright and unguarded, that even Clementine finds herself momentarily stunned.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I believe they would be proud of you. Definitely.
Someone calls for Lydia from the stage. Their time is running short, and she'll have to go soon. But there's still a moment left—just enough time for one more question.

Clementine looks up, trying to see the girl more clearly through her glasses, and through the years that separate them. Perhaps it's because of how sunny it is, but even her hands don't feel as cold as they usually do. A warmth stirs in her chest.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: So then... one last question.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Lydia... are you doing well? Are you happy?
Lydia furrows her brow, thinking it over seriously for a moment.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: Well, sure, there are plenty of little things that don't go my way. But I have so many people who love and support me now, and so many people I love in return. So... my answer is yes. I can say with certainty that I'm happy.
A bell chimes. Lydia waves at the two of you.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: I should get going, there's another event coming up. It was wonderful talking to you both. I hope you'll be happy too!
Lydia hurries off, but then suddenly remembers something after running a short distance. She quickly turns back and unfastens a wind chime charm made of pinecones and seeds from her bag.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: This is for you! I don't know where I picked up the habit from, but whenever I see seeds under trees, I just have to collect them. Over time, they turned into this wind chime. Pretty cute, right?

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: Maybe I'm imagining things, but... it looked to me that when you hear all that clinking and chatter, you seem really at ease.

steps.speaker: Lydia
steps.content: That and you remind me so much of someone! I don't know why, but I just want to keep looking at you, keep talking to you... Anyway, you have to take it! Okay, I'm off now! Bye!

Clementine doesn't even get a chance to refuse. The girl is already gone. She's left standing there with the charm pressed into her hand, and remains frozen in place. Only after a long moment does she slowly lift the wind chime to examine it.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Acorns, hazelnuts, silvered pine cones, lotus seeds... Oh, looks like there are cockleburs and beech nuts too.
The words flow into one of your ears and smoothly out the other.

options: You sure know a lot about this.

choices.text: You sure know a lot about this.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: That's because writing requires all sorts of obscure knowledge. For instance, you could place fungal spores inside these dried pine cones, hang them by a window, and let the spores disperse... excessive inhalation can cause hallucinations, and the sound of the wind chime would only intensify the effect...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I really did not need to know that!
You instinctively pull back from the wind chime in her hand.
Watching your reaction, Clementine finally lets out a genuine laugh, the wind chime jingling brightly in her hand.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Yeah, thanks to you.
Clementine looks in the direction Lydia went.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Lydia... How did you find her after all this time?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: During the investigation, we managed to restore Redwood's old adoption system. The data from before the fire was incomplete, but the records of surviving children remained intact.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The family who adopted her cherished her deeply and kept detailed records of her life. Even though her name changed, that only meant it took a little more time to track her down.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The scar on her arm... it's from the explosion. Even after all these years, I recognized it instantly.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: She hasn't gone far. You could go tell her who you are if you really want.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: No, that would be far too clichéd. My professional standards won't allow it.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What are you saying? A certain someone went through all that trouble to give me the answers, didn't they?
You pull out the small card from your pocket. It's the one with the safe house address written on it.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: With your skills as a renowned author, Clementine, you could've easily hidden your tracks far better than this. You knew I'd find your clues. You knew I'd track you down to your safe house.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...But honestly, did it have to be this complicated?
Clementine only smiles. She says nothing, playing coy. Her gaze drifts toward where the girl headed off to. There, a tree is watching as its seed gets carried away on the wind.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So... you feeling better now?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...As long as I know she's happy. That's enough.

Dusk settles over the campus. Streetlights flicker on one by one. Students pass by in small groups—some calling out to friends, others slipping into the library buildings. On the benches, someone's conversing quietly.
It's time for you both to leave as well, and return to where you belong.
And so, the story comes to an end.

The children heal from their wounds at last, wiping away their tears as they continue down their paths. And she who remained trapped in place for so many years... her time, too, finally begins to move forward.
The spring breeze carries a hint of warmth, lifting the hem of Clementine's coat. She watches the gray figure walking ahead of her.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: <i>${PlayerName}, the truth is... I never got to study here in the end.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: <i>The girl I once was, the one who loved to dream... I thought she'd died in that fire. That all the beauty and hope in the world had vanished with her.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: <i>But... you've given me something new to hope for.
Justice is fairness and retribution, but its ultimate purpose is to spread love, mercy, restraint, and hope.

In time, when the flames burn out, new life will sprout from the scorched earth. Those who were lost will never truly be gone—for there will always be someone who carries their love, their memory, and all they left behind into the future.
The past cannot be reclaimed, but the light ahead remains. That is something worth following.
Clementine walks past you. Her steps are light. She'll carry this steady stride no matter where the road leads.
Fortunately, she likes the view here.
The heart that was once filled with hatred, left hollow after she struck down her enemy, is slowly being filled with new feelings. Just like a wind chime ringing with gentle, pleasant sounds.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: If someday, the redwood seeds could scatter, drifting far and wide to take root elsewhere... Perhaps there, they would become forests that stretch as far as the eye can see, and if you listen closely, you'd hear the gentle chime of wind through the trees...

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...I look forward to seeing that future.
